items.title: Strait of Hormuz closed — live energy shock
items.detail: Iran says Hormuz stays closed and has attacked vessels transiting it this month. Brent settled around $91-93. This is the dominant macro variable right now: it lifts energy names and simultaneously raises the inflation floor, which keeps yields elevated.

items.title: Long-end yields at two-decade highs
items.detail: The 30-year Treasury yield reached its highest level in nearly twenty years. Higher discount rates hit long-duration equities hardest — high-multiple software, pre-profit growth and anything valued on distant cash flows.

items.title: Semiconductor de-rating
items.detail: The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell ~5.6% in one session with all 30 components lower. Whether this is a pause in an intact cycle or the start of an AI-capex reset is the single biggest open question for this book, which remains semi-heavy.

items.title: Narrow leadership has reversed, not broadened
items.detail: Money rotated into energy and defensive healthcare rather than broadening across the market. Rotation markets can mask index-level damage while individual positions break down.

items.title: Oil-driven margin pressure on industrials
items.detail: Higher crude raises input and fuel costs. GE Aerospace fell ~5.0% and the industrials sector ~1.5% — airline customers' economics deteriorate as fuel rises.

items.title: VIX still calm at 15.84
items.detail: Volatility has not confirmed the rotation. That is either reassuring or complacent; if VIX breaks above 25 and stays there, the recession checklist starts lighting up.

items.title: Inflation path re-opened
items.detail: An oil shock feeds directly into headline inflation, which could remove the rate-cut support the market was pricing after the soft July jobs report.
